sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V.Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.31938 of 2015
Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioner, seeking the following relief:
"....to issue a writ order or direction more particularly in the nature of writ of mandamus declaring the action of the 3rd respondent in disbursing the compensation amount in respect of property bearing No.6-3-803/1/15, 6-3-803/1/16 and 6-3-803/1/17, Ameerpet, Hyderabad by virtue of notice No.C3/401/2015 dated 10.07.2015 to 4th and LRs of 5th respondent i.e., 6 to 8 respondent as illegal,
arbitrary against the principles of natural justice and violative of Art. 300A of the constitution of India and provisions of law and consequently declare that 4th and LRs of 5th respondents i.e., 6 to 8 are not entitled to receive the compensation and direct the 3rd respondent not to disburse the compensation amount to 4th and 5th respondents in respect of property bearing No.6-3-803/1/15, 6-3- 803/1/16 and 6-3-803/1/17, Ameerpet, Hyderabad
by virtue of notice No.C3/401/2015 dated 10.07.2015 and pass..."

2. Heard Smt. Pamada, learned counsel representing learned counsel for the petitioner, and learned counsel representing learned Advocate General appearing for the respondents for respondents.
3. Petitioner claims to be the owner and possessor of the premises bearing Nos.6-3-803/1/15,
6-3-803/1/16 and 6-3- 803/1/17 situated at Ameerpet, Hyderabad.
The case of the petitioner is that he acquired the said property under the partition deed executed among the coparceners of the said property.

It is also the case of the petitioner that as per the 2 CVBR,J wp_31938_2015 partition deed, the petitioner was receiving rents regularly and he was also paying necessary charges/taxes to the local authorities.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the said premises was affected in the road widening and the other co- sharers, taking advantage that property stands in their name, made an application to respondent No.3 for receiving the compensation as determined under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, "the Act 30 of 2013").

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is further grievance of the petitioner that since respondent Nos.4 and 5 are not having any right or entitlement over the subject property and as per the partition deed, the petitioner is entitled for the rights over the subject property, which is acquired by respondent No.3 for the purpose of Hyderabad Metro, the petitioner has submitted objections to respondent No.2 not to disburse the compensation amount determined for the property acquired.

But, respondent No.3 is insisting for ownership certificate in spite of all the information and documents and if it is not produced the compensation amount will be paid to petitioner's sister-in-laws as the property is originally stand in their name jointly.

sentences.text: This Writ Petition is pending on the file of this Court since 2015.
The respondents have not filed any counter affidavit.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner vehemently contended that as per the partition deed,
the petitioner is the owner and possessor of the subject property, which is acquired by respondent No.3 for the purpose of Hyderabad Metro Rail and he had also submitted objections to the competent authority, constituted under Section 51 of the Act 30 of 2013, praying not to disburse the amount to other legal heirs.

6. Since it is the case of the petitioner that he is having right and title over the property and objections submitted by the petitioner were pending consideration on the file of competent authority, this Court is of the opinion that the ends of justice would be met, if the competent authority is directed to examine the claim/objections submitted by the petitioner while disbursing the compensation amount in terms of Section 76 of the Act 30 of 2013.

The competent authority is further directed to pass appropriate orders in accordance with law for disbursement of the compensation for their respective shares in the property acquired, after hearing all the concerned share holders.
With the above observations, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
